title: Embedded / IoT firmware intern (EE student)
jd:
Embedded Firmware Intern - Halvard Microsystems

About the role
Halvard designs low-power environmental sensors for cold-chain warehouses.
Our devices run on a single coin cell for a battery life of 2 years, and we
manage a fleet of 10,000 devices in the field. As an intern you will join the
firmware team and write code that runs on real hardware from week one.

What you will work on
You will write and test firmware in C and C++ for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers,
bring up new sensors over I2C and SPI, and help debug issues with a logic
analyzer and oscilloscope. You will also help improve our over-the-air (OTA)
update process and write small Python tools for factory testing.

Who we are looking for
You are studying electrical, computer or embedded engineering, or computer
science. You have written C for a microcontroller (Arduino, ESP32, STM32 or
similar) and understand serial protocols such as UART, I2C and SPI. You can
read a datasheet and a schematic.

Nice to have
Experience with FreeRTOS or another RTOS, Bluetooth Low Energy, low-power
design, and Git.

title: Cybersecurity SOC analyst intern (CS student)
jd:
Northgate CyberDefense is hiring a SOC Analyst Intern for our Bangkok security
operations center. Our analysts monitor 2,500 endpoints for 40 client companies
around the clock, and interns sit with the day shift for a 4-month placement.

You will watch alerts in our SIEM, triage them with a senior analyst, and write
short incident notes. You will look at network traffic, Linux and Windows logs,
and phishing emails, and learn how we escalate real incidents.

We are looking for students in computer science, IT or cybersecurity who are
comfortable on the Linux command line and understand networking fundamentals:
TCP/IP, ports, DNS and HTTP. You should know how to read a packet capture in
Wireshark and be curious about how attacks work. Capture-the-flag experience is
a big plus.

It is a bonus if you have used Splunk or another SIEM hands-on, can script in
Python or Bash, have configured firewalls, or hold Security+ or a similar
certificate.

Send us your resume and a link to any write-ups or home lab notes.
